defs.def: the organ inside the head that controls movement, thought, memory and feeling 脑

ex.s: We are tempted by sugary treats because our ancestors lived in a calorie-poor world, and our brains developed a response mechanism to these treats that reflected their value — a feeling of reward and satisfaction.
ex.t: 我们会被含糖零食诱惑，因为我们的祖先生活在热量匮乏的世界里，而我们的大脑形成了一种对这些零食的响应机制，反映出它们的价值——一种奖励和满足感。

ex.s: But as we’ve reshaped the world around us, dramatically reducing the cost and effort involved in obtaining calories, we still have the same brains we had thousands of years ago, and this mismatch is at the heart of why so many of us struggle to resist tempting foods that we know we shouldn’t eat.
ex.t: 创作活动需要自信。

ex.s: Our formative environment as a species was information-poor, so our brains developed a mechanism that prized new information.
ex.t: 作为人类，我们形成期的环境是信息匮乏的，因此我们的大脑形成了一种重视新信息的机制。

ex.s: Our brains can form multiple long-term goals and ambitions.
ex.t: 五年前我开始转向零浪费生活方式时就经历了这种情况，当时我和父母住在一起；现在我和丈夫一起生活时也继续经历这种情况，因为他并不像我一样完全零浪费。

ex.s: These social emotions prepare our brains to shape our behaviour according to the norms and values of our family and our community.
ex.t: 这些社会情感让我们的头脑做好准备，根据家庭和社区规范与价值观来塑造行为。

ex.s: Why do we dream？Scientists aren't completely sure,and they have diverse____11____ (idea)．Dreams might be a side effect of memory making.When you sleep,your brain sorts through everything ____12____ happened during the day，trying to link new experiences to old memories.As it ____13____ (connect) things，your brain tums them into a story,and you get a dream．
ex.t: 我们为什么会做梦？科学家也不完全确定，他们有各种各样的___11___（想法）。梦可能是记忆形成的副作用。当你睡觉时，大脑会梳理白天发生的每一件事___12___，试图把新经历和旧记忆联系起来。当它___13___（连接）事物时，大脑把它们变成了一个故事，于是你便做了个梦。
